description: Session Overview This workshop will explore different ways in which AI can be incorporated into review workflows, including developing search strategies, grey literature searching, screening, extraction, and writing. We will focus especially on search strategy development using ChatGPT, as well as examine screening tools with varying degrees of automation. This session will also introduce best practices for AI use disclosure and highlight common journal guidelines. Learning Objectives Assess when AI can effectively be integrated into a review workflow Evaluate AI-assisted search strategies for errors and biases Understand how to disclose AI use in accordance with current recommendations and/or journal guidelines Register to receive the Zoom link and password. About the series This session is part of the AI in your Toolkit: Critical approaches to using AI in your work workshop series. About the instructor Eileen Chen, MLIS, is an Education and Research Librarian. She offers support with literature searching, open access publishing, data management, and AI literacy.

description: For decades, molecular biologists have interpreted gene regulation through measurements of mean gene expression, because they could not resolve regulatory variation among individual cells. The advent of single-cell genomics has now made that variation measurable, revealing pervasive differences in gene expression among apparently similar cells. Whether this variation mainly reflects stochastic noise or an informative regulatory property remains unclear. Here we show that mean-corrected gene expression dispersion is a reproducible and biologically structured feature of gene regulation that reflects regulatory fidelity. In heterogeneous differentiated cardiac cultures, genes with low dispersion are shared across cell types, enriched for housekeeping functions, depleted for expression quantitative trait loci, and more highly connected in transcriptional and protein interaction networks. In a comparative single-cell system spanning human, chimpanzee, and allotetraploid cells, a substantial subset of interspecies differences in regulatory dispersion persists in a shared trans environment, indicating that gene expression fidelity is often regulated in cis. Our findings establish gene expression dispersion as a genetically encoded dimension of gene regulation that is distinct from mean expression, and places dispersion along a fidelity-plasticity axis with implications for development, disease, and threshold-dependent cellular phenotypes.

description: Living with meningioma can be a difficult and isolating experience. Many meningioma patients find comfort and strength through connecting and exchanging stories, information, and resources with other individuals affected by a similar diagnosis. This support group is open to UCSF patients with a diagnosis of meningioma. Meetings are facilitated by a neurosurgery nurse and a member of our research staff who work together to create and maintain a safe space to talk and explore important topics, such as: Emotional and mental well-beingSide effect and symptom managementSurvivorship opportunities Treatment optionsResearch developmentsCommunity resourcesFor details and registration: https://ucsf.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KXObcPnKPdeSrA?Q_CHL=qr Please Note: As part of the registration process, your enrollment and continued participation is subject to review by our clinical and administrative team. This helps us ensure that the group is appropriate for you and supports a positive and supportive experience for all members. You will be notified via email once the review is complete and your enrollment is confirmed.

description: All are welcome to attend the 19th Annual UCSF Health Equity and Anti-Racism Research (HEAR) Symposium taking place on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, 8 AM – 3:30 PM, at Mission Bay Conference Center. Register is free. tiny.ucsf.edu/HEAR. This year’s keynote speaker will be Olveen Carrasquillo, MD, MPH. Dr. Carrasquillo serves as Associate Dean of Clinical and Translational Research, Co-Director of the Clinical and Translational Science Center Institute, and Professor of Medicine and Public Health Sciences at University of Miami Miller School of Medicine. His advisory roles include the NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood (NHLBI) Advisory Council; chair of Patient Centered Outcomes Research Institute (PCORI) Clinical Trails Advisory Panel, and chair of the Journal of General Internal Medicine editorial board. Dr. Carrasquillo holds over 25 years leading NIH-funded clinical, community-based health, and multi-center research projects, including as Multiple Principal Investigator (MPI) for the NIH All of Us program. HEAR Symposium offers AI-enabled live translation in 10 languages – smartphone or tablet required. UCSF welcomes all participants to our events. If you need to request a reasonable accommodation to participate in our event due to a disability, please contact Brooks Bigart by emailing brooksley.bigart@ucsf.edu as soon as possible. UCSF endeavors to create greater understanding and supports the exchange of diverse ideas. The views and opinions of guest speakers on campus are their own and may not reflect the perspective of the University. For more information, please visit the symposium webpage: tiny.ucsf.edu/HEAR., powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform
